name: Week 18 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Pull-Up + DB Row)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. Spotlights cycle forward to the pull-up and the DB row — the two heavy pulls, now that the shoulder's a non-issue and grip is the honest limiter, drilled for clean slow-eccentric reps and the grip-capped top set. Loads hold, with a couple of optional gradual nudges where there's headroom and the user isn't holding (face pull, cable crunch climb-back, high cable curl). DB row holds the 70/80/90 bare-hand pyramid — grip is the limiter, no straps. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). Spotlights cycle to pull-up + DB row — the two heavy pulls, drilled now that the shoulder's clear and grip is the cap. DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps. Optional gradual nudges: face pull 50 (if elbows stay high), cable crunch climb-back, high curl 180. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — the shoulder's a non-issue now (W16: 8/8/7/6, 'pretty much no shoulder pain'), so the pull-up earns the deep-cue treatment as the build-the-reps frequency lift. Spotlight drills the active-hang start, elbows-to-ribs pull, and slow eccentric so the floor keeps rising on clean reps, grip + strength the only limiter.

Cycles forward — the heavy pull where grip is the honest cap. Spotlight drills the glued-chest setup on the 70/80 sets and the realistic single-count top set at 90, so the back does the work and the grip taps out before the form does — no straps.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W16 lat pulldown + incline curl · W17 chest-supported row + reverse fly · W18 pull-up + DB row (current) · W19 cycle forward — lat pulldown + face pull refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — the protective counter-movement to all the pulling can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Right after the warmup.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** The top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand taps first) — that's deliberate, train the grip rather than bypass it. Set the DB down when grip gives.
**Grip is the ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, and the push-day farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.

**Optional gradual nudges (you pull these, not me):** face pull 47.5 → **50 if the elbows stay high** with the knuckles-up grip; cable crunch 62.5 → **65-67.5 if the hips-locked form is locked in**; high cable curl 170 → **180 if it moves clean.** Only nudge what feels easy at the current number; otherwise hold. The floor rising is the win, not the number.
**Face pull — knuckles-up grip stays.** Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up; that's what unlocked 47.5 with the elbows still high. If a step to 50 drops the elbows, go back to 47.5.
**Cable crunch — form-first.** 62.5 won back true ab flexion (hips locked, slow eccentric). Earn the climb-back; if the hips start yanking, stay at 62.5.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, reverse fly 20, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance even though the weak-left cleared.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 push warmup + KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension. Primes the pull-up spotlight.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched.

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8 (W16 was 8/8/7/6 — keep building the clean-rep floor).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — clean reps, grip + strength the only limiter now:**
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, shoulders pulled down out of the ears — NOT a collapsed dead hang
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar — think 'drive the elbows into the back pockets'
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping, no kip
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — frequency over max effort; the floor rises on quality reps

**Reflection:** the shoulder's a non-issue now — so does the set end on grip / honest strength, or does form get sloppy (kipping, half-ROM) to make the number? Clean reps are the whole point; bank 6 clean over 8 sloppy.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — DB Row (Spotlight) + Chest-Supported Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the grip-capped heavy pull, drilled:**
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — chest glued to the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze on the 70 and 80** — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, single-count tempo is honest** — grip won't hold a 2s eccentric there, so don't force it; drive the elbow, aim for ~5 clean reps before form breaks rather than grinding sloppy ones
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. No straps — train the grip

**Reflection:** does the grip tap out before the back form breaks (correct — that's the honest cap), or is the back rounding to muscle the 90? If the back goes first, the chest peeled off the pad — re-glue it and let the grip be the cap.

**LOAD:** 40. 3 sets of 10-12.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** the whole set — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides stay on the pad
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom.

**LOAD:**
- **Actual preacher bench when it's open** — EZ bar, ~2×10 on the bar; take the real preacher station whenever it's free, it locks the upper arm better than the incline lean
- **Incline bench, 25lb DBs** (fallback) — chest-supported curl, 3 sets of 8-10

- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad; the upper arm stays flat the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** (DB version) — keep the protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric.

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps.
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — a sweep, NOT a row; the elbow angle never changes
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the hand never lifts first
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep wide, don't lift, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — control the drop. Rear-delt / mid-trap shoulder-health work; quality over the number.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. DB row leads the block (spotlight, run while fresh). 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Dual pulley: 70** (the current home — 'very little pain' here)
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — the honest cap, same as the DB row.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets at 47.5, optional 50)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **47.5** — optional step to **50 if the elbows stay high** with the knuckles-up grip (you pull this; don't force it).
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — that's the change that made 47.5 feel easy with the elbows still high; keep it
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- **If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped** — re-set them high. If 50 drops the elbows, go back to 47.5.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): **170** — optional **180 if it moves clean** (you pull this)
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start.

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 62.5** — the form-first number; optional **65-67.5 if the hips-locked form is locked in** (you pull this)
- **Cable column (rope): scale similarly for form**

3 sets.
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it. Only climb the load if the form holds; if the hips start yanking, stay at 62.5.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that keeps pull day flare-free.
**Spotlight: pull-up + DB row.** Pull-up drills clean active-hang reps (shoulder's a non-issue, build the floor); DB row drills the glued-chest 70/80 + the honest single-count 90, grip as the cap.
**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Top set 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand) and that's deliberate — train it.
**Optional gradual nudges (you pull these):** face pull 50 if elbows stay high, cable crunch 65-67.5 if form's locked, high curl 180 if clean. Otherwise hold; the floor rising is the win.
**Face pull — knuckles-up grip stays.** Drop back if a step to 50 drops the elbows.
**Grip is the ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip. No straps.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, reverse fly 20, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance.
**Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers** — lat pulldown (70 dual pulley / 140 machine / 52.5-57.5 column / 47.5 pulley). Pick what's free, log it.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading. The spotlights drill the two heavy pulls now that the shoulder's cleared — the pull-up as the build-the-floor frequency lift and the DB row as the grip-capped top set — because clean reps with grip as the honest limiter is how the floor rises here, no straps. Loads hold, with a few optional gradual nudges the user pulls where there's headroom. Building decades, not weeks.
